name: Question 2
problem:
Consider the following relation defined on the set $A=\{5,8,10\}.$ 

$$
R=\{(5,5),(5,8),(8,10),(10,5),(10,8)\}
$$

Select the options that make the following reasoning correct:

Since 
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}, 

the relation is 
{{field-3}}.
worked_solution:
A binary relation $R,$ defined on a set $A,$ is 

- *reflexive* if $(x,x)\in R$ for all $x\in A,$

- *irreflexive* if $(x,x)\notin R$ for all $x\in A.$

If some pairs of the form $(x,x)$ belong to a relation and others do not, then the relation is neither reflexive nor irreflexive.

In our case, the relation is defined on $\{5,8,10\},$ and we have

$$
(5,5)\in R,\,(8,8)\notin R,\,(10,10)\notin R.
$$

Therefore, we can conclude the following:

$\,$ Since $(8,8)\notin R$ $\text{and }(5,5)\in R,$ the relation is $\text{neither reflexive nor irreflexive}.$

Consider the following relation defined on the set A={5,8,10}.

R={(5,5),(5,8),(8,10),(10,5),(10,8)} Select the options that make the following reasoning correct:

Since
(5,10)∉R
(5,10)∉R
(x,x)∉R
(x,x)∈R
(8,8)∉R
and (5,5)∈R
and (10,8)∈R

EXPLANATION

A binary relation R, defined on a set A, is

  • reflexive if (x,x)∈R for all x∈A,

  • irreflexive if (x,x)∉R for all x∈A.

If some pairs of the form (x,x) belong to a relation and others do not, then the relation is neither reflexive nor irreflexive.

In our case, the relation is defined on {5,8,10}, and we have

(5,5)∈R,(8,8)∉R,(10,10)∉R.

Therefore, we can conclude the following:

Since (8,8)∉R and (5,5)∈R, the relation is neither reflexive nor irreflexive.
